construct: Enteropeptidase at the duodenal mucosal surface initiates pancreatic protease activation by cleaving trypsinogen to trypsin. Trypsin then activates additional trypsinogen molecules as well as chymotrypsinogen, proelastase, and procarboxypeptidases. Loss of enteropeptidase therefore causes broad protein maldigestion despite preserved pancreatic synthesis of the zymogens.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Normal pancreatic zymogen production with absent active trypsin that is restored by exogenous enteropeptidase identifies failure of the initiating trypsinogen-to-trypsin cleavage step.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Direct activation of chymotrypsinogen by enteropeptidase is tempting because multiple proteases are inactive, but physiologically enteropeptidase activates trypsinogen and trypsin activates the downstream zymogens.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The ex vivo rescue by enteropeptidase and preserved zymogen abundance make the initiating trypsinogen cleavage uniquely supported.
